public_rationale: The measurements show falling average token prices, but do not settle the full claim. Ramp reports spending growth in a weekly comparison, while Vercel identifies a shift toward cheaper models. Neither sample establishes an industry-wide plateau across the selected months. Falling blended prices also do not, by themselves, prove that labs cut comparable prices because of competition.
limitations: The samples are not representative of all industry spending.
Weekly comparisons, monthly totals, and estimated gateway spending are not interchangeable.
The evidence supports a price decline more clearly than the spending or causal assertions.
The unknown accounting basis and unmatched scopes prevent a decisive financial score.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Token spend has plateaued for months, and token prices are collapsing as AI labs cut prices to compete with both closed and open source competitors.

statement.excerpt: Token spend has plateaued for months, and token prices are collapsing as AI labs cut prices to compete with both their closed and open source competitors.

from_speaker: Token spend has plateaued for months
AI labs cut prices to compete
our_interpretation: Token spend means money paid for model inference, rather than token volume, subscriptions generally, or annualized laboratory revenue.
Use August through October 2026, the latest three completed months before publication, as an ordinary reading of 'for months'. Two months is also plausible.
A plateau means no material sustained spending growth; collapsing prices means a large, sustained decline in comparable per-token prices.
Separate posted price cuts from average prices falling because customers choose cheaper models or use different token types.
The causal assertion requires evidence that competitive pressure contributed to providers’ cuts, beyond simultaneous changes in prices and usage.
No company list, currency, accounting basis, or numeric threshold is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Representative monthly expenditure data show a sustained plateau, comparable API prices decline sharply, and provider statements or credible analysis link the cuts to competition from closed and open models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable expenditure data show material sustained growth, comparable prices do not decline sharply, or credible causal evidence refutes competition as a contributor to the asserted cuts.

evidence.locator: Summary; comparison dates in Tokenomics table
evidence.explanation: Ramp reports spending growth between the weeks ending September 25 and October 23, alongside lower blended prices. This qualifies the plateau assertion, but a selected customer sample and two individual weeks cannot establish the industry’s monthly trend.

The gateway sample supports a substantial decline in average prices. Its methodology estimates spending from list prices, and its discussion attributes part of the decline to adoption of cheaper models, so it does not independently prove industry-wide provider price cuts caused by competition.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable monthly spending totals through October, historical model-specific price schedules, and evidence linking material provider cuts to competitive pressure while accounting for changes in customer and model mix.
